newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin calls Baltic NATO membership "dangerous".
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin calls Baltic NATO membership "dangerous".

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Sunday admitting former Soviet Baltic states into NATO would endanger Russian security and Moscow would strongly oppose their admission into the Western alliance.

Yeltsin spoke after meeting Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari just days after a NATO summit in Madrid during which members invited three former Soviet allies -- Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary -- to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.

"I expressed, of course, our dissatisfaction with the Madrid Communique as it mentions the Baltics as new (potential) states and that's dangerous," Yeltsin told reporters. "We will be categorically against this."

After a meeting in St Petersburg on Sunday with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said NATO reserved the option to invite Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia into the alliance.

"We have said all along that NATO is open to all democratic market systems in Europe...It doesn't matter where a country is on the map, they are eligible for membership in NATO," she told Russian television.
